chunks: And everything in this book that is narrated from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira Al-Nadri has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh - may Allah be pleased with him - from his father, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr together, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira Al-Nadri.

key_terms.الْحَارِثُ بْنُ الْمُغِيرَةِ النَّضْرِيُ: Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira Al-Nadri, a companion of the Imams whose narrations are being referenced.
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect used for the narrator.
key_terms.مَجِيلَوَيْهَ: Majilawayh, a prominent scholar and father of the author of this book.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, another key narrator in the chain.
key_terms.يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ: Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman, a key narrator in the chain.

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira Al-Nadri verified in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies the isnad for narrations from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira Al-Nadri by citing his personal transmission through Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, thereby linking the report to the prominent scholarly lineage of the Banu Majilawayh. This explicit mention of his teacher underscores the reliability of the chain and highlights the importance of direct teacher-student transmission (samāʿ) in Shia hadith sciences.
